definition: Major depressive disorder is a condition marked by a noticeable change in how a person is functioning, with at least two weeks of symptoms that include depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure. It also involves several other possible symptoms, such as changes in sleep or weight, low energy, slowed or agitated movement, guilt or worthlessness, trouble thinking or deciding, or thoughts of death or suicide.
